body:
# CSV Viewer UI v2: a full-panel table with Sequel Ace-style filters

Follows #1. Where this SPEC and #1 disagree, this SPEC wins; everything else in #1 still holds.

## Problem Statement

The first release works but reads like a form, not a data viewer. The file name, path, buttons and paging controls are stacked above a small table. Every action is a text button. Paging uses Previous/Next. Columns are resized with Narrow/Widen buttons. Rows are selected through a checkbox column, and a single click copies a cell. Search only matches "any cell contains". Sorting is slow: each 50-row page re-sorts the whole file, so a 5 GB file takes tens of seconds per page.

## Solution

Make the table fill the panel, with two compact rows above it and a status bar below.

1. **Path bar**: `<file name> | <path>`. The file name is for reading only. The path is editable: workspace-relative inside the workspace, absolute outside it. Enter opens the typed path. Esc or leaving the field restores the current path. Errors appear below the bar and the current table stays. With no source, the name is empty and the path shows "Type a path or drop a file".
2. **Icon row**, each icon with a hover tooltip: choose local file, first record is header, refresh, filter (⌘/Ctrl+F), copy selected rows (⌘/Ctrl+C), reveal all hidden columns (enabled only when some are hidden, with a count badge), sort mode (Auto/Numeric/Text dropdown; disabled without a sort; the Auto tooltip shows the detected mode).
3. **Drop anywhere**: the whole panel is a drop target and shows a "Drop to open" overlay. A dropped file replaces the current source without asking. The Open path button goes away.
4. **Status bar**: row count (`1,234 of 5,000,000 rows` when filtered, `Showing 1,200 of …` while scrolling), selected count, source size in 1000-based units with one decimal (`1.2 GB`), and state (`Preparing 45%`, `Sorting…`, `Filtering…`, `Ready`).
5. **Toasts** at the panel's bottom right, for about 2 seconds: "Copied 3 rows", "Copied cell", "Can't select more than 10,000 rows".

### Table

- Infinite scroll with a growing scrollbar: the scrollbar covers only loaded rows. Within one screen of the bottom, the next 200 rows are appended. There is no Previous/Next and no jump to the end. Changing the sort or filter returns to the top.
- Rows are one line, ending in … when cut off. Hovering shows the full value. Double-clicking a row's bottom edge expands it to show everything, and double-clicking again collapses it. Several rows can be expanded. Changing the sort, filter or source collapses them all.
- Column width: drag the header's right edge (minimum 40 px). Double-clicking the edge fits the widest loaded cell or the header, up to 600 px.
- Each header has a ⋮ menu at its right end: Sort ascending, Sort descending, Clear sort, a divider, then Hide column. The current sort state has a ✓, and the sorted header shows ↑/↓. One column is sorted at a time. Clicking the header text does nothing.
- Double-clicking a cell copies its value.

### Selection and copy

- Remove the checkbox column. The row-number gutter stays.
- Click selects only that row, with a grey background. ⌘+click on macOS or Ctrl+click elsewhere toggles a row. Shift+click selects from the last clicked row to this one, in displayed order.
- ⌘/Ctrl+A selects the rows at least partly visible in the viewport.
- Selection is limited to 10,000 rows. An action that would exceed it leaves the selection unchanged and shows a toast.
- ⌘/Ctrl+C copies the selected rows as TSV: visible columns only, no header.
- Selection clears when the sort, filter or source changes.
- ⌘/Ctrl+F, C and A are handled only while the panel has focus. Inside the path and filter inputs they keep their normal text behavior.
- No keyboard row navigation.

### Sort

- Sorting by a column builds the full row order once. Scrolling reads from that order. Choosing a new sort cancels one still being built.
- Numeric mode compares as DOUBLE (ADR 0001). The definition of a number is unchanged. Non-numeric text goes after numbers, blanks last, and ties keep file order.
- DuckDB uses every logical core of the daemon machine with a 4 GB memory limit. With 1 GB, 14 threads ran out of memory while sorting.

### Filter (ADR 0002)

- ⌘/Ctrl+F or the filter icon opens a full-width filter bar under the icon row, with focus on the value. Esc closes the bar and clears the filter.
- Each rule is `[✓] [column ▾] [operator ▾] [value] [−][+]`. Rules combine with Match all / Match any, without nesting.
- The column list starts with "Any column", which covers visible columns only. Hidden columns stay selectable and show `[hidden]`. A rule on a column that becomes hidden keeps applying.
- Operators: contains, does not contain, =, ≠, begins with, ends with, is empty, is not empty, matches regex; and >, <, ≥, ≤, between, which compare as DOUBLE and treat non-numbers as no match.
- Text operators ignore case by default. The `Aa` toggle makes them case-sensitive.
- Enter or the Filter button applies the filter. Toggling a rule's checkbox (on by default) reapplies immediately. A new filter cancels the previous one.
- A switched-on rule whose operator needs a value but has none is ignored and gets a red border.
- The server builds parameterised SQL from the rules. Users never type SQL.

### Preparation

- Blank lines are skipped, not reported as errors. The JS pre-scan of the whole file before loading is removed.
- After the preview, scrolling continues during preparation, reading straight from the CSV. ⌘A, copy, column hide/resize and row expansion also work. Sort and filter are disabled until preparation completes.

### Refresh and resets

- Refresh keeps the sort, filter, hidden columns and widths. It clears the selection and expanded rows and scrolls to the top.
- Toggling the header, or opening another source, resets everything.

## Performance targets

Updated 2026-10-21 (ADR 0003): performance is guaranteed for sources up to 500 MB (500,000,000 bytes), judged by native measurement on real hardware; the emulated Cua VM is used for behaviour and its timings are recorded for reference only.

- Up to 500 MB: first sorted screen within 2 s for Auto, Numeric and Text; each scrolled page within 0.2 s.
- Over 500 MB: before preparing, the panel warns that sorting and filtering can take a long time and opens only after the user confirms (OK / Cancel). No timing is promised; 5 GB numbers are recorded as reference.

## Changes to #1

- Supported size: performance is guaranteed up to 500 MB instead of 5 GB; larger sources open after a confirmation (ADR 0003).
- User stories 27–31 (search): replaced by filter rules. "Search includes hidden columns" now applies only to rules that name a hidden column; "Any column" skips hidden columns.
- Exact numeric sorting: replaced by DOUBLE comparison (ADR 0001).
- Blank-line errors: blank lines are skipped.
- Paging controls, Narrow/Widen buttons, the checkbox selection column and click-to-copy cells: removed.

## Out of Scope

Typed SQL filters. Multi-column sort. Nested rule groups. `IN` lists. Jump-to-end or jump-to-row. Keyboard row navigation. Select-all beyond the viewport. Copying more than the 10,000-row selection limit. The macOS acceptance in #10 runs after this SPEC, on the new package.

## Further Notes

- Vocabulary: `GLOSSARY.md` (Source, File name, Path, Filter, Filter rule, Preview, Preparation, Selection, Sort, Sort mode, Hidden column).
- The execution constraints in the 2026-10-21 handoff still apply: plugin only, no host Paseo changes, and app verification only in isolated Cua environments.
